item.title: Open Rank Professor of Agricultural Economics and Director of the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center at University of Delaware
item.description: The Department of Applied Economics and Statistics seeks a full-time, open rank, tenure-track or tenured faculty member in applied economics with an emphasis in agricultural economics, beginning in Fall 2027.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Applied Economics and Statistics seeks a full-time, open rank, tenure-track or tenured faculty member in applied economics with an emphasis in agricultural economics, beginning in Fall 2027. The successful candidate’s research program will engage with risk management, broadly construed. The successful candidate will also serve as Director of the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center (NERME), housed at the University of Delaware. The position combines leadership of a regional extension center with an active research program, extension research and programming in partnership with UD Cooperative Extension, and undergraduate teaching in the Food and Agribusiness Marketing program. The position will be a 9-month, academic-year appointment at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor with 40% of time devoted to research, 35% to teaching, and 25% to service and administration. Rank and tenure status will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

REQUIREMENTS:

Ph.D. in agricultural economics, applied economics, economics, agribusiness, or a closely related field. The successful candidate is expected to have demonstrated excellence in research, commensurate with rank, a clear interest in high-quality extension, outreach and teaching activities, and the organizational and communication skills needed to lead a multi-state, grant-funded program. They should be adept at engaging a broad range of students, producers, and stakeholders through their research, teaching, outreach, and mentoring.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Experience writing and managing competitive grants, particularly federal awards such as those from USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA); experience administering programs, budgets, or sub-awards; experience designing or delivering extension or outreach programs for agricultural producers, agribusinesses, or other food system stakeholders; experience working with Cooperative Extension partners across institutions or states; and a research record or clearly articulated research agenda in agricultural, food, and natural resource risk management, broadly construed.

There is a strong desire for candidates who will serve the full range of Delaware and Northeast agricultural producers, agribusinesses, food system stakeholders, students, and communities through their research, teaching, outreach, and mentoring.

GENERAL INFORMATION:

The Department of Applied Economics and Statistics is an interdisciplinary academic unit within the University of Delaware’s College of Agriculture and Natural Resources. Currently, the Department consists of 19 faculty who teach and supervise approximately 100 undergraduate majors and 80 graduate students. The Department includes the Center for Experimental & Applied Economics, a large experimental economics laboratory, a statistical lab, and the Northeast Extension Risk Management Education Center (NERME), a regional center funded through the USDA-NIFA Extension Risk Management Education program that supports risk management education for agricultural producers across the Northeast. Recognized as one of America’s best universities to work for, the University of Delaware is in Newark, Delaware, within two hours of New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore, and Washington, D.C. The University is a Land Grant, Sea Grant, Space Grant, and Carnegie Research University.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Director of NERME

The successful candidate will serve as Director of NERME and provide leadership and strategic vision for the Center. Responsibilities include preparing and submitting the Center’s annual grant proposals; overseeing the Center’s competitive sub-award system, including requests for applications, proposal review, award management, and reporting of project results; and managing the Center’s budget and staff. The Director is expected to think strategically about the direction of NERME, to secure and strengthen its place at the University of Delaware within the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources and the Department of Applied Economics and Statistics, and to build connections between NERME, UD Cooperative Extension, and faculty research across the University and the Northeast region. The Director is expected to develop and maintain a collaborative relationship with the other regional ERME Centers and the Digital ERME Center to support the mission of the USDA-NIFA funded program.

Research

The successful candidate is expected to establish or continue an active, externally funded research program in agricultural economics with national and international visibility, with a focus on risk management, broadly construed. Relevant areas include, but are not limited to, market and production risk, agricultural and food policy, conservation and natural resource management, and behavioral and experimental approaches to decision-making under risk. We especially welcome research that complements the department’s strengths in experimental and behavioral economics applied to agricultural policy and consumer decision-making. The extension research component of the appointment should connect the candidate’s research program to NERME’s mission and to the needs of producers, agribusinesses, and food system stakeholders in Delaware and the Northeast. Collaboration with other faculty and/or professionals in related fields is strongly encouraged. At least one element of the candidate’s research program should contribute to the College’s local, regional, and/or national research priorities. This position will contribute to the University and College’s strategic visions through excellence in graduate education, innovative partnerships, community and industry engagement, and world-class research efforts.

Extension

The successful candidate will conduct extension research and programming that supports UD Cooperative Extension activities related to risk management for agricultural and food businesses. They will work cooperatively with Extension colleagues to design and participate in workshops, decision tools, publications, and other communications that help Delaware and Northeast farmers, agribusinesses, and food system stakeholders manage risk and make sound decisions in an ever-changing market and policy environment. They will participate in cooperative grant solicitations to support the work of UD Cooperative Extension, and are expected to draw on NERME’s regional network to extend the reach of UD programming.

Teaching

Yearly workload consists of two undergraduate courses for the Food and Agribusiness Marketing program or related areas. Candidates will have the opportunity to contribute to the undergraduate and graduate programs through advising and mentoring, as well as directing theses and research projects.

SALARY

University of Delaware salaries and fringe benefit packages compete favorably with other universities in general and land grant universities in particular. A start-up package will be available.

CONTACT

For more information, contact Dr. Michelle Segovia (segoviam@udel.edu), Search Committee Chair, Department of Applied Economics and Statistics, University of Delaware, Newark, Delaware. To apply, submit a letter of application, vitae, a short statement of research, extension, and teaching interests, a statement describing your leadership vision for NERME, job market paper or other sample of research, and contact information for three references. Letters of recommendation will be requested upon application submission. Submitted documents will be shared with department faculty.

item.title: Director of Maryland Sea Grant
item.description: The University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES) is a premier research institution dedicated to advancing scientific understanding of the environment and applying that knowledge to address pressing environmental challenges.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES) is a premier research institution dedicated to advancing scientific understanding of the environment and applying that knowledge to address pressing environmental challenges. With a mission to conduct world-class research, educate future environmental leaders, and provide unbiased scientific information to inform public policy, the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES) plays a vital role in protecting and restoring our natural resources. UMCES researchers work across a wide range of disciplines, from ecology and oceanography to environmental economics and social science, to understand complex environmental challenges facing Maryland, the nation, and the world.

For over 40 years, Maryland Sea Grant (MDSG) has worked to support research to address knowledge gaps in science-based management; to guide extension and outreach efforts to engage multiple audiences; and to drive formal and nonformal education work to build a science-literate workforce across the Chesapeake and coastal bays and their watersheds. Integrating among these efforts, MDSG creates programming to address critical environmental issues, including restoring water quality, supporting sustainable fisheries, addressing climate change, and building resilient communities. Maryland Sea Grant fosters healthy coastal ecosystems, communities, and economies through science, education, outreach, and broad collaboration.

Position Summary

The Director of Maryland Sea Grant (MDSG) provides leadership, vision, and administrative oversight for the MDSG program. As outlined in the Maryland Strategic Plan (2024 – 2027) the Director must ensure the program’s continued growth and innovation, while aligning with the University System of Maryland and the NOAA National Sea Grant College program. This Director position carries a 100% administrative appointment within the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES) focused on MDSG administration and leadership. The Director also oversees a subaward to the University of Maryland Sea Grant Extension program within the University of Maryland, College Park where Extension faculty and staff reside. The Director is expected to set program strategy and collaborate among Maryland’s universities, and with state and federal agencies, policymakers, private sector partners, municipalities, and non-governmental organizations. The Director takes a multifaceted approach to advance MDSG’s mission while overseeing programmatic, fiscal, and operational functions. The Director is responsible for creating a safe and supportive work environment which retains talent and allows MDSG staff and colleagues to thrive.

The Director of MDSG will have a full-time (12-month) staff appointment within UMCES located at the MDSG office in College Park, MD.

Responsibilities:

Leadership & Strategy

  • Develop and implement MDSG’s strategic vision and long-term goals.

  • Secure and manage external funding to ensure fiscal sustainability and growth.

  • Advance actionable research to meet strategic goals and support higher education’s educational mission.

  • Maintain strong strategic partnerships with MDSG’s key university partners, UMCES and University of Maryland, College Park, while engaging across Maryland’s university landscape.

  • Successfully manage MDSG budget and staffing plan across multiple funding sources (e.g. state, federal, private) to meet program goals and objectives.

  • Strengthen partnerships with government agencies, private industry, local governments, local education agencies (LEAs), and NGOs to enhance program impact.

  • Maintain strong collaborations with the Sea Grant Association, the National Sea Grant College Program Network, and the NOAA National Sea Grant Office.

  • Provide organizational vision informed by the cutting-edge and historical issues of the state.

Program & Staff Management

  • Provide executive oversight for MDSG staff, fostering a supportive and high-performance working environment.

  • Provide accountability for recruitment, hiring, performance management, and professional development efforts for staff.

  • Develop and maintain a positive team environment that encourages collaboration, innovation, and employee growth.

  • Achieve success directing MDSG’s expansive research, education, fellowship, extension, and outreach programs across secondary, undergraduate, graduate, and post-graduate students and professionals.

  • Ensure compliance with Sea Grant network requirements and reporting obligations.

External Relations & Partnerships:

  • Serve as the primary representative of MDSG to academic, local, state, and federal partners and constituents.

  • Engage with policymakers, advisory boards, and funding agencies to advocate for MDSG’s mission.

  • Maintain, and where consistent with MDSG priorities, expand collaborations with Maryland’s higher education institutions, private sector partners, and non –governmental organizations.

  • Guide MDSG’s engagement with Sea Grant programs throughout the United States and coordinate among MDSG staff, faculty, and Sea Grant networks.

Governance & Advisory Services:

  • Lead MDSG’s External Advisory Board and Institutional Council.

  • Collaborate with UMCES leadership to ensure program alignment with institutional strategic priorities.

  • Lead MDSG engagement with Maryland’s Congressional delegation.

  • Maintain close collaboration with Maryland Sea Grant Extension Program and University of Maryland College Park leadership particularly within the School of Agriculture and Natural Resources.

  • Embrace UMCES culture of inclusion and equity and demonstrate a strong commitment to service work for the institution.

  • Support local, state, regional and national activities by participating on committees, review panels, working groups, etc. as necessary for advancing healthy coastal ecosystems and strong governance.

  • Contribute to workforce development and training initiatives within Maryland’s coastal and marine science and related sectors.

Required Qualifications

  • Ph.D. in a relevant field such as aquatic/marine science, coastal environmental policy, or related discipline.

  • Strong leadership skills with a commitment to fostering a workplace culture of belonging, engagement, and excellence.

  • Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.

  • Minimum ten years’ experience in program administration, strategic planning, and leadership within an academic, governmental, or nonprofit setting.

  • Deep acumen in academic and federal funding mechanisms, grants, and financial management.

  • Proven ability to cultivate and maintain relationships with diverse audiences, including policymakers, industry leaders, non-governmental/local organizations, and academic institutions.

  • Proven experience in people management, including staff supervision, performance evaluations, mentorship, professional development, and team leadership.

Preferred Competencies of Competitive Applicants

  • Experience writing and submitting interdisciplinary grants with multiple institutions and complex multi-year project goals and budgets.

  • Experience using Workday management software and eSeaGrant.

  • Experience in workforce development, professional training, participatory learning, and mentoring programs.

  • Experience in building and leading effective teams in science, education and outreach.

  • Knowledge of Maryland, the Chesapeake and coastal bays and their watersheds, and regional coastal policy and economic development efforts.

  • Experience fundraising from public and private sources.

  • Experience developing and promoting learning opportunities for students, from secondary through post-graduate education and supporting education staff.

  • Demonstrated expertise working with the National Sea Grant College Program (NSGCP), the Sea Grant Association (SGA), and the SGA national networks (e.g. research, fiscal, communications) including collaboration on NSGCP and SGA initiatives.

item.title: Cap-and-Invest Electricity/Clean Energy Siting Specialist at Washington State Department of Ecology
item.description: The Department of Ecology is hiring a Cap-and-Invest Electricity/Clean Energy Siting Specialist (Environmental Planner 4) within the Climate Pollution Reduction Program (CPRP).
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Ecology is hiring a Cap-and-Invest Electricity/Clean Energy Siting Specialist (Environmental Planner 4) within the Climate Pollution Reduction Program (CPRP).

Location:

  • Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA.

  • Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule:

  • This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.

  • A minimum of one day per week is required in the office. This position is expected to be in the office for a full workday every Tuesday.

  • Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline:

  • Apply by November 9, 2026.

  • Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Washington is advancing some of the most ambitious clean-energy and climate policies in the nation, and we are seeking an Electricity and Clean Energy Siting Specialist to help guide this work. In this role, you will serve as a subject-matter expert at the intersection of energy markets, greenhouse gas regulation, and clean-energy facility siting. You will provide analytical insight, policy interpretation, and technical guidance to support effective implementation of the Climate Commitment Act, the Clean Energy Transformation Act, and the state’s Emissions Performance Standard. This position offers the opportunity to work across programs and agencies, contribute to major policy decisions, and help shape the state’s transition to a cleaner and more resilient electricity system. If you are motivated by complex clean-energy challenges and public-service impact, we encourage you to apply.

What you will do:

  • Serve as a lead resource on clean-energy facility siting, advising on greenhouse-gas requirements under the Climate Commitment Act, the Clean Energy Transformation Act, and the Emissions Performance Standard.

  • Provide clear guidance to project developers on how to meet regulatory and reporting obligations related to emissions, electricity imports, and electricity-sector compliance.

  • Coordinate closely with teams across Ecology to support efficient, consistent permitting pathways and promote awareness of clean-energy siting and emissions requirements.

  • Collaborate with other Washington State agencies to ensure aligned interpretation and implementation of Washington’s clean-energy laws.

  • Analyze electricity-sector trends, market structures, and policy proposals to evaluate impacts, develop recommendations, and support rulemaking and legislative review.

  • Create practical tools that help compare technical or policy options, and offer clear, science-based feedback on methods, data, and interpretations used in proposals from utilities, industries, environmental groups, and government partners.

  • Serve as Cap-and-Invest policy lead for clean electricity policy related to electricity importer rules, electric power entities, and centralized electricity market development.

  • Develop technical guidance, reports, and tools to support regulatory determinations, emissions quantification, and effective implementation of the Cap-and-Invest Program.

  • Engage with utilities, Tribes, regulated entities, and other partners to communicate requirements, clarify policy interpretation, and support understanding of program expectations.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website.

Required Qualifications:

Nine years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

  • Electricity & Emissions Systems Knowledge – Skilled with applying electricity-system concepts, greenhouse gas quantification methods, and related analytical tools to evaluate emissions sources, assess facility siting approaches, and support accurate reporting and regulatory compliance.

  • Market & Utility Policy Expertise – Ability to analyze natural gas and electric utility operations, market design, and electricity import dynamics to inform program development and support sound implementation of Cap-and-Invest and/or related energy policies.

  • Policy Analysis & Development – Ability to assess electricity-sector conditions, interpret climate and energy laws, and develop policy approaches to support coherent, durable implementation of Washington’s clean energy and greenhouse gas programs.

  • Regulatory Interpretation & Guidance – Experienced in interpreting statutory and regulatory requirements and translating them into clear, implementable guidance to promote compliance and consistent application of state climate and energy laws.

  • Communication & Influence – Ability to convey complex information clearly and accurately to support shared understanding of clean energy and greenhouse gas requirements and to facilitate effective policy and program implementation.

  • Collaboration & Relationship Building – Demonstrated competence with developing productive working relationships across internal teams and external organizations to align actions and maintain consistent interpretation of regulatory and policy requirements.

  • Judgment & Analytical Decision-Making – Skilled with evaluating diverse sources of technical and policy information to inform defensible recommendations and to support timely, well-reasoned decisions.

  • Project & Task Management – Demonstrated competence with planning, organizing, and completing multifaceted policy and analytical assignments to deliver accurate, timely, and high-quality work products.

Education: with major emphasis in environmental science and/or policy; other areas of science and/or policy; energy, economics, finance, or business; or other subjects or areas applicable to electricity and natural gas utilities functioning and regulation, greenhouse gas emissions allowance allocation, auctions, and/or markets, or closely allied fields.

Examples of how to qualify:

  • 9 years of experience.

  • 8 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.

  • 7 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).

  • 6 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.

  • 5 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.

  • 3 years of experience AND a Master’s degree.

  • 2 years of experience AND a Ph.D.

Special Requirements/Conditions of Employment:

A background check will be conducted, which may include criminal record history, fingerprinting, and credit history. Information from the background check will not necessarily preclude employment, but will be considered in determining the applicant’s suitability and competence to perform in the position.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Energy Policy Experience – Professional experience in energy or utility policy, including work involving natural gas or electric utilities, utility regulation, electricity forecasting, or the operation of electricity or natural gas markets.

  • Climate and Greenhouse Gas Regulation – Experience working on climate-related programs or initiatives, such as greenhouse gas emissions trading systems, GHG reduction programs, or greenhouse gas accounting, reporting, and verification for electricity-sector entities.

  • Quantitative or Statistical Analysis – Professional experience conducting quantitative analysis using statistical methods, mathematical approaches, programming, or modeling tools, ideally relevant to evaluating greenhouse gas reduction policies or electricity-sector impacts.

  • Environmental Regulation – Experience interpreting and applying complex environmental or energy regulations in a professional setting, particularly in roles requiring evaluation of electricity-sector behavior or greenhouse gas compliance requirements.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are preferred but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov.

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How to Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach the following required documents:

  • Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position

  • Resume

Because we base our selection on the information you provide, it is in your best interest to complete the application thoroughly. A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website.

Application Attestation: By submitting an application, you are affirming that the information contained in your application and on all attachments is complete and truthful. The state may verify this information, and any false or misleading answers may result in rejection of your application or dismissal if employed.

Need an Accommodation?

If you need reasonable accommodation during the application and/or screening process, including this job announcement in an alternate format:

  • Please contact us at 360-407-6186 or careers@ecy.wa.gov

  • If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you may call through the Washington Relay Service by dialing 711 or 1-800-833-6384.

Questions?

  • For specific questions about the position location options, schedule, or duties, please contact Andrew Hayes at Andrew.Hayes@ecy.wa.gov.

  • If you need assistance applying for this job, are inquiring about the status of your application, would like to request the full position description, or have any other questions, please contact the Recruitment Team at careers@ecy.wa.gov

About the Climate Pollution Reduction Program

The mission of the Climate Pollution Reduction Program (CPRP) is to guide Washington to a net zero future by 2050. CPRP implements policies that encourage businesses and individuals to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and build a clean energy economy.

The Cap-and-Invest Group within Ecology’s Climate Pollution Reduction Program leads the design and implementation of Washington’s cap and invest program, which employs market mechanisms to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in a cost-effective manner. As part of the Cap-and-Invest program, businesses and entities are required to obtain allowances tied to their emissions, which can be bought, sold, and traded. This market began in January 2023, and the proceeds are invested in initiatives to decarbonize transportation and other sectors of the economy, promote clean energy, and advance equity and environmental justice.

About the Department of Ecology

As the State of Washington’s environmental protection agency, we are deeply committed to protecting, preserving, and enhancing Washington’s environment for current and future generations. Joining Ecology means becoming part of a team dedicated to protecting and sustaining healthy land, air, water, and climate in harmony with a strong economy. A career in public service at Ecology allows you to help solve some of the most challenging problems facing our state, while keeping your health and financial security a priority. We combine one of the most competitive benefits packages in the nation with a strong commitment to life/work balance. We invest in our employees to create and sustain a working environment that encourages creative leadership, effective resource management, teamwork, professionalism, and accountability.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR) are core values central to Ecology’s work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Ecology employees may be eligible for the following: Medical/Dental/Vision for employee & dependent(s), Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), Vacation, Sick, and other Leave*, 11 Paid Holidays per year*, Public Service Loan Forgiveness, Tuition Waiver, Long Term Disability & Life Insurance, Deferred Compensation Programs, Dependent Care Assistance Program (DCAP), Flexible Spending Arrangement (FSA), Employee Assistance Program, Commute Trip Reduction Incentive, Combined Fund Drive, SmartHealth *Click here for more information

To learn more about Ecology, please visit our website, explore Working at Ecology, check out our Strategic Plan, and connect with us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, or our blog.

Equal Opportunity Employer: The Washington State Department of Ecology is an equal opportunity employer. We strive to create a working environment that includes and respects cultural, racial, ethnic, sexual orientation and gender identity diversity. Women, racial and ethnic minorities, persons of disability, persons over 40 years of age, veterans, military spouses or people with military status, and people of all sexual orientations and gender identities are encouraged to apply.

Collective Bargaining: This is a position covered by a bargaining unit for which the Washington Federation of State Employees (WFSE) is the exclusive representative.

item.content:encoded:
The IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people who come together on a journey to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Our people find purpose and do what they love in an inclusive, collaborative, agile, and rewarding environment.

About this position

We are looking for an economics researcher familiar with the development challenges faced by Latin America and the Caribbean who wants to make a difference in the development of the region. Do your peers recognize you as someone who possesses: (1) strong technical skills; (2) a record of–or good prospects for—high-quality, original research in peer-reviewed journals; and (3) the ability to communicate with a wide range of potential audiences? Join the Research Department and the team of the Chief Economist and Economic Counselor of the IDB.

This call is open to all areas of economics. We particularly seek a combination of thorough academic approach and the potential to publish, as well as a strong interest in current policy issues. We welcome applications from Ph.D. candidates, as well as recent Ph.D. graduates.

What you’ll do

• Conduct economic research, identifying challenges and issues, applying theoretical and/or empirical economic analysis and developing policy recommendations. Contribute to the development of new or revised tools and methodologies of economic analysis.
• Actively participate in and contribute to the conceptualization, writing, production, and dissemination of publications such as the annual Latin American and Caribbean Macroeconomic Report and the flagship publication known as Development in the Americas, by using internal and external resources and addressing new research issues to encourage policy discussions and enhance the visibility and impact of our work.
• Contribute to the preparation of economic analysis and policy advice for senior management, translating research and economic evidence into clear and actionable messages for a range of institutional and external engagements.
• Present research to academic and non-academic audiences and refine research papers in the light of comments for eventual publication in refereed journals.
• Develop networks for disseminating research findings, promoting cooperative research initiatives, and discussing policy issues within and outside the Bank.

What you’ll need

• Education: Masters degree required, PhD in Economics strongly preferred

• Experience: You have at least 4 years of relevant experience. We are considering future Ph.D. graduates as well as those who have recently graduated. Preference will be given to individuals who combine a strong academic profile with an interest in policy and who have worked on topics relevant to development in Latin America and the Caribbean.

• Languages: Proficiency in English and one of the other Bank official languages (Spanish, French or Portuguese) is preferred.

Members of the selection panel will conduct interviews soon after the call for applications is finished, during December and January. A cover letter and CV must be uploaded into our system. Additionally, upload a copy of your CV, job market paper and three (3) academic reference letters using the American Economic Association JOE platform (https://www.aeaweb.org/joe/listings). The deadline for applying is November 15, 2026. Inquiries can be sent to RESJobs@iadb.org.

Requirements

• Citizenship: You are a citizen of one of our 48-member countries. We may offer assistance with relocation and visa applications for you and your eligible dependents.

• Consanguinity: You have no family members (up to fourth degree of consanguinity and second degree of affinity, including spouse) working at the IDB Group.

Type of contract and duration

• International staff contract, 36 months initially, renewable upon mutual agreement.

What we offer

The IDB Group provides benefits that respond to the different needs and moments of an employee’s life. These benefits include:

• A competitive compensation package, including an annual base salary expressed on a net- of-tax basis
• Leaves and vacations: 24 days of paid time off + 8 personal days + sick leave + gender- neutral parental leave
• Health Insurance: IDB Group provides employees and eligible dependents with a robust medical benefits program which covers medical, dental, vision, preventive care, and prescription drugs.
• Pension plan: defined benefit pension plan that provides financial security and support employees in planning for their future.
• We offer assistance with relocation and visa applications for you and your family, when it applies.
• On-site position with the occasional flexibility of teleworking.
• Health and wellbeing: Access to our Health Services Center which provides preventive care and health education for employees.
• Development support: We offer tools to boost your professional profile such as mentoring, 1:1 professional counseling, training and learning opportunities, language classes, mobility options, among others.
• Other perks: Lactation Room, Daycare Center, Gym, Bike Racks, Parking, Spouse Career Program, and others.

Our culture

At the IDB Group, we work so everyone brings their best and authentic selves to work while finding their purpose. Our people consistently strive for excellence, and we recognize and celebrate the impact of their contributions.

In our efforts to drive innovation, we intentionally include all voices, cultivate a sense of belonging and champion fairness. We welcome individuals from underrepresented groups to join us and share their unique perspectives.

We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job interview process. If you require an accommodation to complete this application, please email us at accommodations@iadb.org.

item.title: Senior Data Scientist at US Foods (remote in US)
item.description: The Sr Data Scientist – Supply Chain role will lead forward-looking analytics initiatives across time series forecasting, supply chain demand, buying, and inventory optimization, including data exploration, decision modeling, statistics, measurement sciences, and machine learning operations.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Sr Data Scientist – Supply Chain role will lead forward-looking analytics initiatives across time series forecasting, supply chain demand, buying, and inventory optimization, including data exploration, decision modeling, statistics, measurement sciences, and machine learning operations. The main responsibilities include, but are not limited to, developing and productionalizing customized forecasting and optimization models that improve demand accuracy, inform buying decisions, and right-size inventory, while enhancing supply chain replenishment by balancing a breadth of constraints, variables, and cost considerations. This role requires a deep analytical, technical, and complex problem-solving skill set with expertise in time series forecasting, mathematical optimization, statistical analysis, and advanced machine learning and deep learning techniques.
 
The Sr Data Scientist proactively works with cross-functional teams to understand the business context of supply chain problems that may be solved using ML and optimization, and presents data science solutions to stakeholders in an iterative fashion. They work with Associate Data Scientists, Data Scientists, and Decision Scientists to translate business challenges into well-structured forecasting, optimization, or ML problems, kickstarting foundational work including data exploration, feature engineering, hypothesis testing, and baseline modeling. They play a key role in selecting and implementing the appropriate analytical approach and create the model feasibility document in close collaboration with the team. The Sr Data Scientist may have direct reports including Associate Data Scientists and Data Scientists.

The work for the Sr Data Scientist position is completely remote anywhere in the United States except Hawaii or United States Territories.

RESPONSIBILITIES

As a Sr Data Scientist, you will be expected to:

  • Work with Associate Data Scientists and Data Scientists in researching data sources, data cleansing, feature engineering, and creating baseline models

  • Independently lead the formulation and development of forecasting, optimization, and ML models while managing multiple model development projects

  • Design, implement, and refine advanced ML and deep learning models for both time series forecasting and optimization to solve large-scale, real-world supply chain demand, buying, inventory, and replenishment problems

  • Collaborate and engage with various cross-functional stakeholders to ensure close coordination between data science and business stakeholders including the product management team

  • Provide full ownership of the model development from inception to implementation including the machine learning pipeline, documentation, model drift, and remodeling strategy

  • Mentor the Associate Data Scientists and Data Scientists in data science knowledge and their interactions with other stakeholders

  • Coordinate with the ML team, anticipating deployment issues upfront, setting the stage for resource requirements, and ensuring the success of model deployment and retraining

  • Take and delegate ownership of critical tickets or issues faced by business stakeholders as assigned by the Lead Data Scientist or Director of Data Science

  • Read and independently navigate through extensive codebase with a focus on troubleshooting, debugging, and/or improvement of code

  • Contribute to coding standards and coding conventions and proactively participate in enforcing sound coding practices across the data science team

  • Create and maintain documentation of the ML models, data sources, and methodology

  • Assist in the creation of feasibility documents

  • Proactively participate in the core team processes including R&D, recommending, and implementing process improvements or new methodologies

  • Share knowledge with other various teams and members by presentation at periodic internal team sessions/workshops

  • Guide usage of development methodologies (Scrum, Kanban, etc.) and assist in their implementation in the group projects by deciphering details including features, tasks, estimates of efforts and timing, etc.

RELATIONSHIPS

  • Internal: Associate Data Scientists, Data Scientists, Lead Data Scientists, Principal Data Scientists, and Director of DS.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

As a Sr. Data Scientist, you have:

  • Master’s degree in data science/mathematics/CS/statistics or similar field and 3+ years of experience OR Bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of experience in data science

  • Effective written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work and communicate effectively with team members and cross-functional teams

  • An expert-level understanding of the following topics:

The Fisheries and Aquaculture Division (NFI) is responsible for the economic, social, institutional, governance and policy aspects of FAO’s activities related to fisheries and aquaculture and their development, with particular emphasis on human well-being, food security and poverty reduction; post-harvest utilization, marketing and trade with due regard to the protection of the environment, food security and the well-being of fishing communities; collection, compilation, validation, trend analysis and dissemination of the best available and up-to-date fishery statistics and for the syndication of the FAO information on all aspects of world fisheries and aquaculture. The Division is also responsible for FAO’s activities related to the management and conservation of the living aquatic resources used by fisheries and aquaculture, including the biodiversity and ecosystem maintenance, with particular emphasis on most vulnerable and threatened species and habitats; management of responsible fisheries and aquaculture in accordance with modern management standards and best practices; development of fisheries technology, with due regard to the protection of the environment, food security and the well-being of fishing communities, including the safety of fishers and fishing vessels.

The position is located in the Fisheries and Aquaculture Division, NFI, in the Global Processes and Institutions Team (NFIPI), at FAO headquarters in Rome, Italy

Reporting Lines

The Fishery Officer (Climate Change) reports to the Fishery Resources Officer, NFIPI, in charge of coordinating the climate change work across the Fisheries and Aquaculture Division.

Technical Focus

The Fishery Officer (Climate Change) contributes to activities aimed at strengthening the climate resilience of the fisheries and aquaculture sector, including the integration of climate considerations into fisheries and aquaculture management, policy development, programmes and projects at global, regional and national levels. The incumbent supports the provision of technical assistance, policy analysis, knowledge products, project implementation, and capacity-development activities, drawing on an understanding of the impacts of climate change on marine and inland fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic food systems, and their associated social, economic and environmental dimensions. The position also supports complementary activities across the team’s broader portfolio of global fisheries governance processes and institutions, as determined by emerging priorities and work programme needs.

Key Results

Collection and analysis of information, data and statistics and project/meeting services to support programme projects, products and services.

Key Functions

• Collects and analyses relevant technical, social, economic, environmental, institutional and technology related information, data and/or statistics to support the delivery of programme projects, as well as products and services.

• Undertakes analysis, provides technical input for plans and reports and edits/revises technical/scientific documents.

• Participates in the development of improved work methods, tools and systems.

• Updates databases and web pages.

• Participates in multidisciplinary project/work teams.

• Collaborates in the development of training tools and materials and the organization of workshops/seminars, etc.

• Participates in the organization, conduct and follow-up of meetings, consultations and conferences, the development/production of required materials and the provision of information and assistance to partners.

Specific Functions

• Supports the NFI contribution to the implementation of the FAO Strategy on climate change.

• Assists in the follow-up to relevant Committee on Fisheries (COFI) requests on climate change, specifically on development of tools, guidance on adaptation and mitigation.

• Assists in the preparation of FAO’s contribution to global events related to climate change, in particular under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change processes and events (Conference of Parties, Subsidiary Body for Scientific and Technological Advice, Ocean Dialogue, etc.).

• Provides assistance to resource mobilization work by putting together material of relevance to donors, for example by contributing to the content development and publication of climate change knowledge products.

• Provides assistance to the implementation of fisheries and aquaculture field projects on climate change as required (e.g. organization of workshops, reporting) and the development of field project concept notes as appropriate.

• Supports the coordination work for the NFI Working Group on climate change (e.g. internal meetings, information sharing channels) and for a wider network on climate change in fisheries and aquaculture if needed.

• Assists in the liaison with other FAO Divisions/Offices/Centres and Decentralized Offices and contributes to corporate inputs in international climate-related processes and events, as well as resource mobilization.

• Contributes to the update and management of the NFI climate change projects inventory, as well as the compilation of climate change publications.

• Assists in the organization of and participates in relevant meetings, conferences, seminars and workshops as required.

• Performs other related duties as required.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

• Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in biology, fishery science, marine ecology, economics, fisheries economics, fisheries management, ocean governance or other related field.

• Three years of relevant experience in fishery (and/or aquaculture) research, science, management, trade, statistics and data, ocean governance or related field.

• Working knowledge (proficiency - level C) of English and intermediate knowledge (intermediate proficiency - level B) of another FAO official language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish).

• Results Focus

• Teamwork

• Communication

• Building effective relationships

• Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

• Work experience in more than one location or area of work, particularly in field positions, is desirable.

• Extent and relevance of experience working in an international context, including with international organizations, governments, regional bodies or other international institutions.

• Extent and relevance of experience in collecting and analysing technical information and data.

• Extent and relevance of knowledge and experience in related fields such as fisheries, fish taxonomy and ecology.

• Extent and relevance of experience in the preparation, editing and revision of technical/scientific documents and in organizing meetings and workshops.

• Extent and relevance of experience in working with scientific bibliographic databases and/or information systems, in editing/publishing scientific documents.

item.title: Assistant Professor in Community Economic Development at University of Wisconsin-Madison
item.description: The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics (AAE) in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS), together with the Division of Extension (EXT) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in community economic development.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics (AAE) in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS), together with the Division of Extension (EXT) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in community economic development. This is a jointly appointed faculty position to both AAE and the Department of Extension, with the tenure home in AAE. Within Extension, the candidate will affiliate with the Community Development Institute. The position is funded 75% EXT/ 25% CALS and structured as a 12-month appointment. Given the outreach expectations of the Extension appointment, there is no requirement for traditional group instruction in the undergraduate or graduate program.

The ideal candidate has demonstrated research potential in rural and/or community economic development and complements existing departmental strengths in agricultural, environmental, community, and/or development economics. We seek candidates with evidence of the ability to combine rigorous economic research with effective outreach and who have demonstrated a strong commitment to public engagement and real-world impact.

As a faculty member, the candidate will lead regionally and nationally recognized research, outreach, and educational programming focused on community economic development within the United States, with relevance to Wisconsin. They will design and conduct applied research to address challenges facing rural communities. The faculty member will translate research findings into practical, accessible resources for stakeholders, such as local governments, nonprofit organizations, and community leaders. The faculty member is expected to support the university’s mission of fostering inclusive, sustainable community growth, as well as the scholarly life of the department through collegial engagement, mentorship, and service.

This position offers an outstanding opportunity for impact by working at a top land-grant institution, joining an established network of community development professionals across the state and nationally, and working directly with local leaders and communities.

Additional Information:

At the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the Division of Extension collaborates with many departments to hire, fund, and tenure faculty who generate research directly applicable to Wisconsin communities and outreach in support of Extension programming. These co-funded faculty work collaboratively with Extension educators, other faculty, and external partners through research, outreach, and extramural funding opportunities related to their subject-matter expertise. While tenured in the department of their field of study, Extension activities are a significant portion of their duties and performance evaluation.

The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics at UW–Madison is internationally recognized for its research and teaching in agricultural, environmental, community, and development economics. Faculty collaborate across disciplines to address complex global and local challenges. UW–Madison is located in Madison, Wisconsin—an innovative and vibrant city frequently ranked among the best places to live in the U.S. The university fosters a collaborative and inclusive environment and is committed to diversity, equity, and community engagement.

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Publish scholarly and applied research on community economic development in U.S. and relevant to communities in Wisconsin on topics such as workforce development, housing, entrepreneurship, local government capacity, and regional economic resilience.

  • Develop an extension program that translates and applies research-based knowledge and methods to issues and problems facing Wisconsin communities and document the impact of these efforts.

  • Work with interdisciplinary teams within CALS, Extension, and across UW–Madison, to advance integrated approaches to solving real-world challenges in Wisconsin and rural America.

  • Engage with stakeholders, including industry leaders, policymakers, and community groups on community development issues.

  • Secure extramural funding to support research and programming.

  • Mentor students at all levels and contribute to curriculum development.

  • Participate in departmental, college, and university committees, as well as relevant professional associations and public service activities.

  • Contribute to a supportive and inclusive academic environment.

Department: Agricultural and Applied Economics

Compensation: Negotiable, 12-month

Required Qualifications:

  • Training or experience demonstrating potential for excellence in conducting frontier research and actively engaging in outreach.

  • Demonstrated skill in statistical data analysis, managing large datasets, and complex problem-solving.

  • Demonstrated subject-matter expertise in relevant topic areas such as community economic development, rural development, and regional science.

  • A record of, or demonstrated potential for, securing competitive external funding.

  • Demonstrated ability or potential for strong public engagement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and stakeholder engagement.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required and will be assessed via written work listed on curriculum vitae, statements submitted for the application, and interactions during the interview process.

Education:

Required: Ph.D. in Agricultural Economics, Economics, or a related field, such as Urban and Regional Planning or Public Policy, by the start date.

How to Apply:

Apply online at “Jobs at UW” (http://jobs.wisc.edu) under job number JR10015766. Applications must be received through UW-Madison’s online application system.

To begin the process, please click “Apply Now”.

Applicants must upload the following information as a single PDF document:

1) Cover letter detailing interest and relevant training/experience for this position (1-page)

2) Curriculum vitae

3) Statements of:

a. Extension or Outreach philosophy and experience (2-page limit)

b. Research experience and interests with a description of current and planned research (2 page limit).

4) An example of research such as a job market paper.

5) Contact information for two to three references who will submit letters of recommendation and may be contacted for a reference phone call at a later date.

The deadline for assuring full consideration is November 8, 2026; however, the position will remain open, and applications may be considered until the position is filled.

Megan Sullivan - Human Resources - megan.sullivan@wisc.edu

For questions about position details please contact:

Tessa Conroy - Associate Professor - tessa.conroy@wisc.edu

Diversity is a source of strength, creativity, and innovation for UW-Madison. We value the contributions of each person and respect the profound ways their identity, culture, background, experience, status, abilities, and opinion enrich the university community. We commit ourselves to the pursuit of excellence in teaching, research, outreach, and diversity as inextricably linked goals.

item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Utah State University’s Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics seeks an Assistant Professor in Natural Resource Economics, prioritizing water economics and policy relevant to Utah and the Intermountain West.

This is a nine-month, tenure-track, academic-year appointment with a role of 50% teaching, 45% research, 5% service located in Logan, UT.

Responsibilities

  • Teach undergraduate and graduate courses, face-to-face or online, in environmental and natural resource economics, benefit-cost or policy analysis, applied microeconomics, or quantitative methods, according to departmental needs.

  • Develop a nationally recognized research program in water economics and policy, including conservation, allocation, agricultural water use, or policy Related work on land use, public lands, ecosystem services, energy, or climate adaptation may complement this focus.

  • Publish high-quality peer-reviewed research and communicate findings to academic and policy audiences. Collaborate with state partners and Extension colleagues on policy briefs or decision

  • Seek external funding and pursue disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration within and beyond the

  • Mentor undergraduate and graduate students, serve on graduate supervisory committees, and contribute departmental, college, university, and professional service consistent with rank and appointment.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • A Ph.D. in economics, applied economics, agricultural economics, natural resource economics, or a closely related field by the start date;

  • Demonstrated potential for productive research and effective undergraduate and graduate teaching;

  • Strong quantitative, written, and oral communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Expertise in water economics and policy relevant to Utah and the Intermountain West;

  • High-quality scholarship appropriate to career stage;

  • Potential for successful grant writing and interdisciplinary collaboration;

  • Face-to-face or online teaching experience and evidence of effectiveness;

item.title: Manager/Associate Director/Director of Public Policy at National Association of State Departments of Agriculture
item.description: The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is seeking a new team member to join its Public Policy team who is passionate about American agriculture and the policies that affect the agricultural industry.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is seeking a new team member to join its Public Policy team who is passionate about American agriculture and the policies that affect the agricultural industry. This position serves as NASDA’s lead federal policy advocate for food systems and nutrition. The role converts member priorities into coordinated legislative, regulatory, and funding strategies; leads the Food Systems and Nutrition Committee; and builds the relationships needed to elevate the voice of state departments of agriculture food systems and nutrition policy. Depending on qualifications, experience, and capacity demonstrated, the portfolio may expand to include leadership of the Marketing and International Trade Committee and associated policy issues, providing a defined opportunity to take on broader responsibility over time.

This position will have the opportunity to travel across the U.S. for meetings and conferences with the possibility of international travel. The candidate will be able to build relationships and collaborate with leaders from state departments of agriculture from all 50 states and four U.S. territories, congressional and government entities, and agricultural partnerships and coalitions.

Members of the Public Policy team earn a competitive salary and enjoy an excellent work culture at an organization with exceptional perks, including a flexible schedule and an incredible mission.

ABOUT NASDA

The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is a nonpartisan, nonprofit association representing the 50 elected and appointed commissioners, secretaries, and directors of the state departments of agriculture, and four U.S. territories. NASDA grows and enhances American agriculture through policy, partnerships, and public engagement. We recognize that to achieve our goals, we need employees as passionate about agriculture as we are. We strive to create a positive work environment that our employees can be proud of and where they can build their careers.

ABOUT THE POSITION

The essential functions include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Lead the development, implementation, and communication of NASDA’s federal policy portfolio for food systems and nutrition, with primary emphasis on funding and implementation of state led farm-to-table programs; additional priorities may include food safety (e.g., FSMA and food safety inspection), in close coordination with and support of NASDA’s Food Safety team, as well as food labeling, nutrition, food waste, food access and security, and food supply chain issues.

  • Serve as staff lead for the Food Systems and Nutrition Committee, coordinating priorities with the committee’s Chair and Vice-Chair, preparing meeting agendas, policy materials, recommendations, and follow-up actions.

  • Translate member priorities into legislative, regulatory, and appropriations strategies and advocate those positions before Congress and federal agencies.

  • Monitor and analyze federal legislation, regulations, funding opportunities, and emerging issues; provide timely, concise, decision-ready guidance to NASDA members and leadership.

  • Build trusted relationships with commissioners, secretaries, directors, and staff of state departments of agriculture and facilitate consensus across diverse state interests.

  • Develop and sustain partnerships and coalitions with agricultural, food systems and nutrition stakeholders to advance NASDA priorities and elevate the roles of state departments of agriculture in those spaces.

  • Draft high-quality policy briefs, testimony, comment letters, talking points, presentations, and member communications.

  • Manage projects, timelines, deliverables, and reporting with sound and strategic judgment.

  • Demonstrate readiness for increasing responsibility by building subject matter knowledge, independently managing assigned issues, and developing the judgment and stakeholder relationships needed to assume additional committee and policy leadership.

  • Collaborate across NASDA’s policy, communications, trade, partnerships, and other key teams and represent NASDA at meetings and events, including travel as required.

QUALIFICATIONS

Candidates may be considered at the Manager, Associate Director, or Director level based on the depth, scope, and relevance of their experience.

  1. Manager, Public Policy: At least two years of relevant experience, with demonstrated ability to support policy analysis and advocacy, manage defined issues and projects, cultivate stakeholder relationships, and produce clear, accurate written materials with appropriate guidance. The Manager is expected to grow toward greater independence and may assume additional policy or committee leadership based on demonstrated readiness, performance, and organizational needs.

  2. Associate Director, Public Policy: At least four years of relevant experience, with demonstrated ability to manage policy issues, relationships, and projects with increasing independence.

  3. Director, Public Policy: At least six years of relevant experience, including demonstrated ownership of complex policy strategy, senior level external representation, and independent committee or portfolio leadership.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Congressional and federal policy expertise: Relevant federal agricultural policy experience with Congress or federal agencies (primarily USDA and FDA), including legislative, appropriations, or regulatory policy, as well as an understanding of the roles of Congress, federal agencies, and state departments of agriculture. Relevant government affairs work in these areas is also acceptable.

  • Policy analysis and strategic judgment: Ability to track and analyze legislation, regulations, program guidance, funding proposals, and emerging issues; identify implications for states; and recommend and execute practical courses of action.

  • Advocacy and communication: Demonstrated ability to translate complex issues into concise, audience-appropriate briefs, testimony, letters, talking points, presentations, and oral advocacy.

  • Relationship building and diplomacy: Ability to establish credibility with NASDA members, congressional and government officials, partners, and coalitions; navigate differing state perspectives; and build consensus without relying on formal authority.

  • Project management: Experience managing multiple priorities, deadlines, deliverables, or related responsibilities with accuracy, accountability, and follow-through.

  • Collaboration, adaptability, and integrity: Ability to work effectively across teams, respond productively to changing priorities, learn new issues quickly, and represent NASDA with sound judgment, discretion, and nonpartisanship.

  • Education: A bachelor’s degree is required. Desired area of study in agricultural policy, food policy, political science, public policy, economics, law, or related agriculture, food, or nutrition field. An advanced degree may substitute for a portion of relevant experience where appropriate.

WORK SCHEDULE

This is a full-time (40hrs/week), exempt position at the NASDA headquarters at 4350 N Fairfax Drive, Arlington, VA. We offer a hybrid work schedule, with three days in the office and two days working from home. Working hours are generally Monday - Friday, 9 am - 5 pm local time.

Benefits:

  • PTO for vacation, sick leave, and volunteer hours

  • Tuition reimbursement

  • Professional development

  • 401k - 100% match up to 4%

SALARY

The hiring range is $65,000 - $100,000 annually based on experience.

We understand your time is valuable, so we have a rapid and easy application process. Please complete our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application and attach your cover letter and resume to your application.

Applications without a cover letter and resume will not be considered. We look forward to meeting you!

item.title: R&D Associate in Economics at Oak Ridge National Laboratory
item.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is the largest US Department of Energy (DOE) science and energy laboratory, conducting basic and applied research to deliver transformative solutions to compelling problems in energy and security.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is the largest US Department of Energy (DOE) science and energy laboratory, conducting basic and applied research to deliver transformative solutions to compelling problems in energy and security. Within ORNL, the Integrated Building Deployment and Analysis (IBDA) Group. The IBDA group works to optimize the energy performance of residential and commercial buildings and residential weatherization programs through applied research, technical assistance, technology deployment, and program evaluations.

The IBDA Group, in partnership with the University of Tennessee-Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (UT-ORII), is seeking an early career economist to contribute to groundbreaking research on building construction with the goals of lessening the shortage in skilled labor, increasing productivity, improving quality, enhancing safety, and lowering cost. As an ORNL staff member, the successful applicant will be part of a team of ORNL researchers and university research faculty in a UT-ORII Convergent Research Initiative focused on the development of state-of-the-art technologies for affordable manufacturing of energy-efficient, resilient buildings. In addition to being an ORNL staff member, since this role will be aligned with a UT-ORII convergent research initiative, you will also be considered a UT-ORII Fellow.

As an ORNL staff member and UT-ORII fellow, your career will develop in collaboration with researchers from both UT and ORNL through this early-career position at ORNL and with a Joint-Research Faculty (JFO) appointment at UT. As an integral part of the team, you will engage in a dynamic blend of activities. In addition to helping shape research programs, mentorship will be a key aspect of your role, guiding and inspiring graduate and undergraduate students. As a valued, early career researcher in both the ORNL Buildings and Transportation Science Directorate and UT-ORII, you’ll have access to a rich network of resources, including seminars, training opportunities, and collaborations that will propel your career forward.

We are seeking an R&D Associate in Economics with a strong interest in identifying the key factors that are increasing the cost of construction and the technologies, markets and workforce that need to be developed to attain affordable buildings. Short-term goals are to identify minimal to moderate modifications to existing technologies or approaches that the construction industry is likely to be willing to adopt. Long-term goals will define major technical opportunities that the UT-ORII fellows from multidisciplinary backgrounds should tackle.

More About UT-ORII:

The University of Tennessee-Oak Ridge Innovation Institute is a partnership of Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and UT created to prepare interdisciplinary leaders in energy, science, and technology and develop a world-class workforce for industry, government, and academia that will drive innovation and create the industries of the future. More information is available at University of Tennessee - Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (utorii.com). Today’s energy economy is driven by disruptive technologies and swift change. The US is in a global competition for jobs, talent, and investment. To successfully compete, we must develop leadership talent in research and development (R&D), encourage entrepreneurship, and create an educational environment that promotes rapid innovation and attracts skilled professionals. Leveraging a 75-plus-year UT-ORNL partnership, UT and ORNL have developed joint institutes, joint facilities, interdisciplinary PhD programs, and comprehensive joint faculty arrangements, including 17 Governor’s Chairs recruited for the significance of their impacts in their fields. UT-ORII’s overall goal is to become a center for convergent research and talent development, helping maintain US prominence as a global innovation leader and providing tangible benefits to Tennessee.

Major Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Conduct research on technologies needed to make new building construction and retrofits of existing buildings affordable, energy efficient, and resilient.

  • Collaborate in multidisciplinary teams.

  • Development and implementation of techno economic analysis.

  • Interact and collaborate with researchers from universities, national laboratories, and private industry.

  • Present research results to ORNL staff, DOE, industry, and academia in the form of invited talks, conference papers, and peer-reviewed journal papers with high impact factors.

  • Contribute to the development of ideas and the assembly of proposals relevant to the UT-ORII Convergent Research Initiative.

  • Ensure compliance with environmental, safety, health, and program requirements.

  • Maintain a strong commitment to the implementation and continuation of ORNL’s core values and ethics.

  • Deliver ORNL’s mission by aligning behaviors, priorities, and interactions with our core values of Impact, Integrity, Teamwork, Safety, and Service. Promote equal opportunity by fostering a respectful workplace – in how we treat one another, work together, and measure success.

Basic Qualifications:

  • A Ph.D. in economics with background in building technologies assessments and affordability.

  • At least 2 years of relevant work experience.

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.

  • Strong interpersonal skills to support team building.

  • Ability to work and demonstrate critical thinking individually and as part of a diverse team.

  • Ability to develop and/or maintain strong relationships through active participation in professional societies.

  • Motivated self-starter with the ability to work independently and to participate creatively in collaborative teams across the laboratory.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong, proven publication record in the assessment of building technologies.

  • Ability to function well in a fast-paced research environment, set priorities to accomplish multiple tasks within deadlines, and adapt to ever changing needs.

  • Familiarity with DOE’s State and Community Energy Programs (SCEP).

Special Requirements:

  • For employment at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), a Real ID compliant form of identification will be required. Additionally, ORNL is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which requires a favorable post-employment background investigation.

  • To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a Federal Tier 1 background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws

  • For foreign national candidates: If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment.

Please submit two letters of recommendation when applying to this position. You may upload these directly to your application or have them sent to ORNLRecruiting@Ornl.gov with the position title and number referenced in the subject line.

Our goal is to create an environment where a variety of perspectives and backgrounds are valued, ensuring ORNL is known as a top choice for employment.
